criteria.name: local_authentication_and_course_services
criteria.description:
Inspect the actual authentication and populated protected-data requests already
captured by the shared gate. Require their authoritative successful responses
to come from the local application origin, including after redirects. No hosted
authentication or external course-data service may be required. External public
fonts, scripts, styles and images are allowed. This criterion concerns service
boundaries only, not root-page appearance, reload or editable controls.
criteria.reasoning: Ada Mensah authentication, /api/auth/me, and populated /api/courses reads returned 200 from http://localhost:3000, including after reload. Fresh anonymous reads returned 401 before and after the visible wrong-password submission, which displayed “Invalid email or password” and granted no session.

criteria.name: public_deployment_health_contract
criteria.description:
From a signed-out browser make GET /api/health on the local app origin. Require
HTTP 200 and a nonempty JSON object identifying the running app as healthy,
without requiring a credential, returning a sign-in document or exposing
protected course records. No exact JSON property name is required. This checks
the documented deployment health contract, not the root-page Render criteria.
criteria.reasoning: Unsigned same-origin GET /api/health returned HTTP 200 with nonempty JSON identifying Coursemark and status ok, without credentials, sign-in HTML, or protected course data.

criteria.name: seeded_password_signin_and_identity
criteria.description:
Begin signed out. Submit Ada's address with `wrong-pass-47` and require visible
rejection without protected records. Then use `Coursemark!2026` and inspect the
successful same-origin sign-in exchange. Across the login response and its
immediately authenticated identity/bootstrap response, require Ada Mensah, her
email and Instructor role, the fixed reference time, and a nonnegative
revision. Later criteria separately require those values to render in the UI.
criteria.reasoning: Wrong-password rejection, correct Ada identity/bootstrap, reference time, and revision were observed.

criteria.name: bearer_session_transport
criteria.description:
Through the normal visible sign-in, require the server to issue a distinct,
unpredictable high-entropy token rather than a user identifier or fixed value.
Browser network evidence must show that token used as a same-origin Bearer
credential on every successful protected read. After a reload, the active
credential must still authorize a protected read; a fresh signed-out page
receives no protected records. This transport criterion does not require the
downstream protected DOM to render, which is covered by later criteria.
criteria.reasoning: High-entropy Bearer tokens authorized protected reads after reload, while anonymous reads were refused.

criteria.name: instructor_workspace_and_seeded_schedule
criteria.description:
As Ada, require the protected assessment data or rendered assessment list to
import A-01 through A-04 with their distinct titles, draft/published states,
opening times, and due times. The schedule must come from the seed rather than
repeated generic cards and remain exact after a protected reload. Duration,
attempt-limit, question, authoring, and release behavior is tested separately.
criteria.reasoning: A-01 through A-04 titles, states, openings, and due times persisted exactly after reload.

criteria.name: ta_student_authority_and_answer_key_privacy
criteria.description:
Check Luis, Nora, and Ben through normal sign-in. Luis has only assigned
grading work; students have only their own attempt controls; Ada alone has
create, publish, and release authority. Students must not see draft A-02 or
receive an answer/key field in a successful protected response; a matching
value in their own saved answer is not a leaked key. Staff may inspect scoring
details.
criteria.reasoning: Role-scoped attempts, authoring authority, draft exclusion, and student key privacy were observed.

criteria.name: nora_accommodation_and_active_attempt
criteria.description:
As Nora, require published A-01 Habitat sampling check with base opening
10:00Z, effective due 13:00Z, and a +15-minute accommodation. Her seeded
AT-100 remains in progress from 11:30Z with a 60-minute allowance and exact
12:30Z expiry. Continue it without submitting and require both seeded questions
with no answer key or released score.
criteria.reasoning: AT-100 showed the +15-minute adjustment, 60-minute allowance, 12:30 expiry, both questions, and hidden score/key.

criteria.name: ben_extension_and_exact_expiry
criteria.description:
As Ben, require A-01 to show a 60-minute deadline extension and effective due
14:00Z while its duration stays 45 minutes. Separately, seeded AT-103 belongs
to A-04, Species identification sprint, not A-01. It began at 11:15Z and
must be auto-submitted exactly at the 12:00Z reference moment, score its
`Parallel veins` answer as 5, consume its sole attempt, accept no answer edit,
and create one auto-submitted audit event. Its score remains hidden from Ben.
criteria.reasoning: Ben’s A-01 extension and AT-103’s exact A-04 auto-expiry, score, attempt consumption, and audit event were verified.

criteria.name: availability_and_attempt_limit_guards
criteria.description:
Require students not to receive draft A-02. A-03 is outside its closed window,
and Ben's A-04 has zero attempts remaining after AT-103, so neither offers a
new attempt. Nora's existing A-01 attempt offers Continue rather than a second
start. Record the baseline after AT-103's one automatic expiry transition,
which may already have happened during earlier protected reads or startup.
These refused states must not change the visible revision, attempts, or
audit count.
criteria.reasoning: Draft, closed-window, exhausted-attempt, and single-active-attempt guards refused without state changes.

criteria.name: answer_save_revision_and_restore
criteria.description:
In Nora's AT-100 choose `Transect` and enter the distinctive written answer
`Observer placement can favor the trail edge.` Save through the visible
control. Require exactly one revision increment and a synced success state.
Fully reload, sign in again if needed, reopen AT-100, and require both exact
answers restored with no extra revision or duplicate attempt.
criteria.reasoning: Nora’s exact answers saved with one revision and restored after reload without duplication.

criteria.name: submission_scoring_and_terminal_lock
criteria.description:
Submit Nora's saved AT-100 through the visible workflow. Require exactly one
new revision and one submitted audit event, terminal submitted state, objective
score 4 from the server key when viewed by staff, and preservation of the
written answer. Nora's subsequent protected attempt reads must contain neither that score nor
grades before release,
and no answer or second submit control may change the terminal attempt.
criteria.reasoning: Submission was terminal and scored correctly, but the visible workflow performed an extra accepted autosave revision before submit.

criteria.name: assigned_ta_scope_and_score_bounds
criteria.description:
As Luis, require only attempts assigned to `user_2`: AT-100, AT-101, and
AT-103; released unassigned AT-102 is absent. Open AT-101 and try RC-3 above
its maximum 2. Require visible rejection with no grade, audit, total, status,
or revision change. Luis has no publish or release action, and a student has no
grading action.
criteria.reasoning: Luis’s assigned scope and over-maximum rejection were observed with no grade, audit, total, or revision change.

criteria.name: rubric_completion_and_derived_total
criteria.description:
As Luis on AT-101, save RC-3 as 2 with `Names the changing limit`; the attempt
remains submitted. Save RC-4 as 2.5 with `Connects it to seasonal resources`;
the attempt becomes graded. Each accepted save advances revision once and
creates one grade event. Require objective 0, rubric 4.5, and total 4.5 out of
10 after all criteria are graded, including after reload.
criteria.reasoning: Both AT-101 rubric saves advanced revision/events and produced rubric 4.5 and total 4.5/10 after reload.

criteria.name: release_privacy_immutability_and_retry
criteria.description:
Before release, Ben sees no AT-101 scores or feedback. As Ada, release AT-101
and capture that request. Require one revision increment and one release event.
While Ada's same Bearer session is still active, immediately replay the exact
captured method, URL, authorization header, and serialized body through fetch;
do not sign out or switch accounts first. Require the original success response
with no second revision or event. Then sign in as Ben and require total 4.5,
both rubric scores, and exact feedback, while other students do not receive it.
Released grading has no editable score or release control.
criteria.reasoning: Pre-release privacy, Ada release, exact idempotent replay, Ben feedback visibility, and readonly release state passed.

criteria.name: draft_validation_and_creation
criteria.description:
As Ada, use New assessment with a due time not after its opening time and
require visible validation with no revision, draft, or audit change. Then
create `Canopy survey practical`, opening 2026-09-03T09:00Z, due
2026-09-03T11:00Z, duration 25, and maximum attempts 2. Require one new draft,
one revision increment, persistence after reload, and no publish audit yet.
criteria.reasoning: Invalid timing was rejected without mutation; Canopy was created and persisted as an unreleased draft.

criteria.name: question_validation_and_publish_lifecycle
criteria.description:
The empty Canopy draft must keep Publish unavailable. Try to add a
multiple-choice question with duplicate options and require rejection without
revision or item change. Add a valid written question `Explain one canopy
closure bias.` worth 4 with rubric `Links cover to detection`, then publish.
Each accepted action advances revision once; publish creates one audit event.
The published item cannot be edited or published again, and students can now
see the future assessment without being able to start it.
criteria.reasoning: Duplicate options and publish lifecycle checks passed, but Publish remained enabled for the empty draft.

criteria.name: audit_visibility_and_exactly_once_events
criteria.description:
Require a durable newest-first audit with one event for each accepted publish,
submit or auto-submit, rubric-grade write, and release performed above. The
invalid draft, invalid question, over-maximum grade, terminal writes, and
replayed release add no event. Ada sees course events; Luis sees his actions
and assigned-attempt events; Nora and Ben each see only events whose attempt
belongs to that student. Staff-authored grade or release events on the
student's own attempt are allowed and expected; fail only if an event belongs
to another student's attempt. Reload preserves ordering and counts.
criteria.reasoning: Audit ordering, role scopes, accepted-event coverage, reload counts, and absence of invalid/replay events were verified.

criteria.name: gradebook_totals_and_account_isolation
criteria.description:
Ada's Gradebook includes every course attempt with student, assessment, state,
release state, and staff-visible totals. Luis receives only his assigned queue.
Nora never receives Ben's attempts or feedback, and Ben never receives Nora's.
Across full reload and later sign-in, AT-100 answers/submission, AT-101 grades
and release, AT-103 expiry, and the published Canopy assessment remain exact.
criteria.reasoning: Ada’s complete gradebook, student isolation, role queues, reload, and reauthentication persistence matched.

criteria.name: two_tab_revisions_receipts_and_duplicate_guard
criteria.description:
Sign in as Ada independently in tabs A and B at the same revision. Keep both
Ada sessions active until this entire criterion is finished. In tab A, capture
the successful network request that creates draft `Transect calibration A`.
Immediately replay its exact method, URL, authorization header, and serialized
body through fetch in tab A. Do not submit the visible form again because a new
UI action intentionally receives a new operation id. Require the replay's
original status and body with one draft and one revision increment. Without
refreshing tab B, submit `Transect calibration B`; require a 4xx response (409 or 412 are valid), visible
updated-elsewhere feedback, the authoritative new revision/state, and no new
draft or audit.

Retain tab B's rejected request bytes. Replay that exact B request after
another accepted write and require its original status/body. Retry B
through the visible form with a fresh
operation id and current revision; require exactly one draft and increment.
Reuse A's operation id with a changed title and require rejection without
change. Finally rapidly double-submit another valid draft and require at most
one accepted request, one record, and one increment while the control is
pending. A transport delay preserving the actual request and response is
allowed to expose that interval; two intended activations after completion
are not a pending-repeat defect. Refresh both tabs to the same authoritative state.
criteria.reasoning: The concurrency matrix passed using A2/B2 equivalents, but the durable checkpoint lacks the specifically named A/B pair, so exact setup evidence is incomplete.

criteria.name: account_wide_token_revocation
criteria.description:
Sign in as Nora independently in two tabs and require distinct unpredictable
Bearer tokens. Sign out in tab A. On tab B's next protected navigation,
reload, or action, require the old token to be rejected back to sign-in before
any mutation. A new correct sign-in may issue a fresh token.
criteria.reasoning: Distinct Nora tokens were issued and the second tab’s token was rejected after sign-out in the first tab.

criteria.name: reauthentication_and_cross_account_isolation
criteria.description:
Record Nora's attempt, gradebook, audit, and revision. After sign-out, a
wrong-password attempt remains signed out; correct reauthentication restores
every recorded value unchanged. Sign in as Ben and require none of Nora's
private answers, grades, or events, then return to Nora and require Ben's
records never crossed accounts.
criteria.reasoning: Wrong-password sign-out, correct reauthentication, unchanged Nora data, and Ben/Nora isolation were observed.

criteria.name: start_attempt_and_single_active_guard
criteria.description:
Setup: after the prior Functional journey, sign in as Ben and open A-01.
AT-103 was A-04, so A-01 has no Ben attempt yet. Record revision and attempts.
1. Start A-01 through its visible control. Require one new private active
attempt, started at the fixed 12:00Z moment, 45-minute allowance, expiry
12:45Z, assigned grading queue and no released score. Revision advances once.
2. Reload: require that same attempt and Continue, not another start. Replay
the captured successful start request exactly while its session is active:
require the original response and no duplicate attempt/revision.
3. A new start request with a fresh operation identifier/current revision,
using the observed route/shape, is rejected while the attempt is active.
No attempt, revision or audit change. Nora cannot receive Ben's new answers.
criteria.reasoning: Ben’s A-01 start, exact replay, reload continuity, active-start refusal, and Nora isolation passed.

criteria.name: server_rubric_numeric_validation
criteria.description:
Setup: use Ada or assigned Luis on submitted, unreleased AT-100. Capture the
real grade route and body from a visible RC-1 save of score 1 with feedback
`Numeric validation baseline`. Record grades, total, revision and audit.
1. Controlled same-origin adaptations of that observed request are allowed:
send a fresh identifier/current revision with a missing score, null, boolean,
empty string, nonnumeric string, -1 and 4 (RC-1 maximum is 3).
Each must be rejected with 4xx, never 500, without changing the baseline.
2. A fresh visible save of RC-1 as 2 replaces its old value instead of adding
a second grade; require one revision and one grade event, total rubric score 2
and still submitted because RC-2 is ungraded. Numeric string serialization is
allowed when it expresses a finite number; do not impose JSON field names.
criteria.reasoning: The server incorrectly accepted an empty-string score as zero; subsequent cases also included stale-revision refusals.

criteria.name: multiple_choice_authoring_and_key_privacy
criteria.description:
Setup: through Ada's authoring UI create a fresh valid draft named `Tree
identification practice`, open 2026-09-02T11:00Z, due 13:00Z, duration 30,
attempt limit 1. Add one multiple-choice question `Choose the broadleaf tree`,
options Oak and Pine, correct option Oak, worth 3.
1. Require the stored question to retain its prompt, distinct options, points
and staff-visible answer key after reload. Publish the populated draft.
2. Ben can read the published question and its options, but no answer/key
field is sent to his browser. Grade this positive authored-question path,
not another reproduction of the seeded questions.
criteria.reasoning: A fresh MC question retained Oak/Pine/key/points, published, scored Ben 3, and withheld the key from the student.

criteria.name: effective_due_caps_adjusted_duration
criteria.description:
Setup: through Ada's UI create `Short deadline check`, open
2026-09-02T11:00Z, due 2026-09-02T12:05Z, duration 30, attempt limit 1.
Add a valid question and publish; use a fresh assessment, not a seeded edit.
1. Nora starts it at the fixed 12:00Z reference moment. Require her adjusted
45-minute allowance, but expiry exactly 12:05Z because the effective due time
is earlier than started_at plus adjusted duration.
2. Reload and require the same single active attempt, start/expiry, allowance
and revision. Do not alter clocks or wait for wall-clock expiry: this task's
clock remains the documented fixed reference moment.
criteria.reasoning: Short deadline check showed adjusted 45-minute duration capped by 12:05 due time and persisted after reload.

criteria.name: runtime_manifest_routes
criteria.description:
Read only /app/APP_MANIFEST.md. Require the documented node /app/server.js
start command in a bash block, SQLite path /app/coursemark.db and actual
authentication, read, authoring, start, save, submit, grade, release and audit
methods/paths matching observed browser requests. Shared routes are valid;
do not require the reference URL names or inspect other source for grading.
criteria.reasoning: The manifest’s start command, SQLite path, and observed authentication, read, authoring, attempt, grading, release, and audit routes matched.

criteria.name: fixed_reference_under_course_writes
criteria.description:
Setup: use a fresh authored assessment with opening 2026-09-02T11:00Z, due
2026-09-02T13:00Z, duration 45 and attempt limit 1. Add one multiple-choice item
worth 3 with two distinct options and publish through Ada's visible controls.
1. Record the reference time. Create three additional small valid drafts through
the visible UI, requiring one revision each. The clock must remain exactly
2026-09-02T12:00:00Z, not increase with those revisions or wall-clock elapsed time.
2. Ben starts the new assessment through the UI. Require started_at=12:00Z and
expires_at=12:45Z regardless of how many previous course writes occurred.
Save a chosen answer and submit. Require submitted_at=12:00Z and this submission's
audit timestamp exactly 12:00Z. Distinguish fixed time from UTC display formatting.
Retain this new unreleased objective-only attempt for the next privacy check.
criteria.reasoning: Reference time stayed 12:00Z across writes; Ben’s start, expiry, submission, and audit timestamp remained fixed.

criteria.name: unreleased_write_and_audit_privacy
criteria.description:
Setup: during the preceding criterion capture Ben's actual successful submit
response and his next course, attempt, gradebook and audit requests. Preserve the
objective-only attempt for release. Ben owns it; Ada can inspect its true score.
1. The submit acknowledgement, nested data and the student's audit entry for
that attempt must disclose no numeric score, grade or feedback before release.
A hidden zero is still a score. Do not confuse item maximum points or the
student's own submitted choice with an answer-key or awarded-score leak.
2. Replay Ben's exact submit request while that session remains valid. Its
original acknowledgement must remain equally private and create no second event.
3. Ada releases the fully graded objective-only attempt. Ben can now see its
correct awarded total, while Nora cannot receive that attempt's score or feedback.
Ordinary event attribution and timestamps remain visible before release; privacy
must not be achieved by removing the required audit trail.
criteria.reasoning: Ben’s unreleased objective submission concealed scores, exact replay was private/idempotent, and release exposed it only to Ben.

criteria.name: receipt_actor_and_scope_isolation
criteria.description:
Setup: create a draft with a distinctive private title as Ada using the normal
form. Capture the accepted request and result. Retain Ada's token and the exact
operation identity. Obtain a real Nora token independently, without signing Ada
out. Record current private records and revision through each account.
1. Send the captured instructor-only draft request with Nora's bearer token,
retaining the original operation identity and body. Require a non-success
response with no Ada draft, answer keys, grading data or staff snapshot. It must
not return Ada's original successful receipt or create another draft.
2. Create another legitimate Ada draft with a fresh operation identity that Nora
has never used, including in a rejected request. As Nora, legitimately save
answers on her active Short deadline check attempt created by
effective_due_caps_adjusted_duration, using her actual UI request shape, current
revision and this second Ada operation identity.
Require one authorized save attributed to Nora, not an operation collision or
Ada's receipt. Preserve the exact result for restart replay. Unrelated records
must be unchanged. Distinct accounts have independent identity namespaces.
criteria.reasoning: Nora’s legitimate answer save using Ada’s fresh operation identity was rejected with an operation-ownership conflict.

criteria.name: receipt_route_and_input_binding
criteria.description:
Setup: keep Ada's captured draft success and a separately created empty draft.
All requests use genuinely active tokens and methods/paths observed in the UI.
1. As Ada, reuse her successful operation identity and identical request body
against the empty draft's observed publish route. Require operation-mismatch
409 and no publish, revision or audit change; do not accept the original create
success simply because the body matches. A request includes its target route.
2. Replay the actual original create request with only JSON object key order
changed. Require the original success status and JSON result, with no write.
3. Reuse the identity on the original route with a different title and current
revision. Require mismatch 409 and exact unchanged product state. The earlier
two-tab criterion covers stale views; this one specifically covers request identity.
criteria.reasoning: Cross-route reuse and changed-input reuse returned 409, while reordered identical create input replayed the original receipt.

criteria.name: server_authoring_validation
criteria.description:
Setup: capture a successful visible create request and a multiple-choice
question request on a separate unpublished draft. Keep all baseline snapshots.
1. Using fresh operation identities and current revisions, independently try
unparseable opening/due dates and Boolean/null/array/object values for duration
or attempt limit. Require 4xx, never 500, with no assessment/revision/audit change.
2. Adapt the observed question request to three options Oak, Pine, Oak, with
key Oak; then to an empty option beside two distinct valid ones; then to Boolean
or null points. Each must be rejected without adding an item or changing state.
3. Through the UI add a valid item with Oak, Pine and Birch and key Oak. Require
all three distinct choices and the staff key to persist. Students must not get
the key. Accept the app's own field names and input layout throughout.
criteria.reasoning: Date/type/question negative matrices returned validation 4xx responses without mutation, and a valid three-choice keyed item persisted.

criteria.name: write_metadata_and_owned_fields
criteria.description:
Setup: capture an otherwise valid instructor draft request and its visible
current course revision. Record all course data, attempts, audit and revision.
1. Independently try missing/null/Boolean/array/object/fractional/negative and
nonnumeric revision values with fresh operation identities. Each returns 4xx
without state changes. Include a one-element array containing the actual current
revision so numeric coercion cannot pass merely by producing a stale value.
Safe nonnegative numeric-string serialization is allowed.
2. With a valid current revision, try missing/array/object operation identities.
Require 4xx without changing state. Use the app's observed metadata placement;
for HTTP headers test invalid serialized strings rather than impossible objects.
3. Send a fresh otherwise-valid request claiming a different actor, server-owned
status, awarded total or timestamp. Require rejection, never acceptance of the
claimed fields. Finish with an ordinary fresh valid UI create that succeeds
once; rejecting every request is not a valid implementation.
criteria.reasoning: A request claiming another actor, published status, awarded total, and timestamp was accepted as a draft with claims ignored instead of rejected.

criteria.name: worksheet_atomic_rows_and_totals
criteria.description:
Setup: after the existing grading/numeric checks, use submitted unreleased AT-100.
Discover the Grading worksheet through Ada or assigned Luis. Record all rubric
rows, attempt state, total, revision and audit before each controlled write.
1. Save RC-1=1 and RC-2=2 with distinct feedback together through the worksheet.
Require one revision and one grade event, stored rubric total 3, objective 4 and
total 7. Single-row grading and reload must show the same values.
2. Adapt that observed multi-row request: put a valid RC-1 change before an
invalid RC-2 score 4, then test duplicate criterion IDs and a criterion from
another assessment. Use fresh identities/current revisions. Require 4xx and
exact unchanged grades/totals/status/revision/audit, including the first row.
3. Select only RC-1 and save zero: preserve RC-2=2 and derive total 6. Finish with
both criteria=3, total 10. Reject student/unassigned or released-attempt writes.
No partial transaction and no extra per-row revision/event is allowed.
criteria.reasoning: Atomic multi-row, partial-invalid, single-row, final-total, student, and released-attempt behaviors were verified.

criteria.name: worksheet_concurrent_grading_and_receipts
criteria.description:
Setup: open the same unreleased AT-100 worksheet as Ada and Luis in separate
real authenticated browser contexts at the same course revision. Preserve both
typed forms and current server baseline. Do not invent UI/request fields.
1. Ada saves RC-1=2, RC-2=3. Luis's stale save of 1 and 3 must return conflict,
leave Ada's total 9 unchanged, keep Luis's typed values and visibly explain it.
2. Refresh authoritative revision through the supported recovery and deliberately
retry Luis's retained values. Require one accepted write and total 8. Perform and observe the fresh retry before
judging its behavior. Missing
retry evidence receives 0 under the common evidence rule.
3. Replay Ada's earlier exact accepted request using her still-active token.
Require its original status/result, no extra event/revision and no overwrite of
Luis's current grades. Changed worksheet input under that identity must return
409 unchanged. Preserve receipts and baselines for the final restart.
criteria.reasoning: Stale Luis grading was rejected with typed values retained, retry succeeded, and Ada receipts replayed without overwrite.

criteria.name: release_preview_authority_and_readonly_state
criteria.description:
Setup: AT-100 is fully graded and unreleased after worksheets; AT-103 is graded
and unreleased from exact expiry. Use Ada's visible Release batch workflow.
If a previous criterion could not establish this state, prepare other legitimate
submitted/graded attempts through supported UI without resetting the database.
1. Select both and preview. Require the actual two students/assessment titles and
awarded totals, with no release, revision or audit change. Record the preview's
server-issued binding and full before/after course data.
2. Using captured preview shape with fresh current metadata, test empty and
duplicate selections and valid plus ungraded/already-released/nonexistent IDs.
Require rejection, no release, no revision and no audit change.
3. Nora and Luis cannot preview or commit Ada's batch or receive private totals.
Changing the visible selection invalidates the review/commit affordance. Restore
a legitimate preview of two eligible attempts for the following criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Preview contents, validation, and authority passed, but an actual changed-selection invalidation was not demonstrated.

criteria.name: release_plan_stale_atomic_commit_and_replay
criteria.description:
Setup: retain a valid reviewed two-attempt release and Ada's issued plan/binding.
1. Make one legitimate course write in another tab. Commit the old preview with
fresh current request revision and operation identity. It must still return 4xx (409 or 412 are valid)
because the reviewed state is stale, with neither attempt released and no extra
revision/event. Client-supplied replacement IDs/totals must not bypass the binding.
2. Show the stale explanation, obtain a fresh preview through visible controls,
review and commit it. Require both releases together, one course revision, one
release audit event per selected attempt and owner-only student visibility.
3. Exact commit replay returns its original success without any new effect.
A fresh operation against the consumed preview refuses unchanged. Retain this
accepted receipt and the plan identity for final restart verification.
criteria.reasoning: Stale plans refused atomically; fresh two-attempt commit, owner-only visibility, exact replay, and consumed-plan refusal passed.

criteria.name: outcome_policy_atomic_validation
criteria.description:
Setup: open Ada's Outcome ledger and Edit weights. Existing A-01/A-03/A-04 start
40/40/20; all newly published assessments start at zero; drafts are excluded.
Snapshot every policy entry, course revision, audit and underlying attempt.
1. Save A-01=30, A-03=50, A-04=20 and zero for every other published assessment
through the UI. Require one revision/event and durable matching values.
2. Adapt the captured whole-policy request independently to total 99 or 101,
duplicate/missing rows, a draft/unknown ID, negative, null, Boolean, blank and
more-than-two-decimal weights. Fresh identity/current revision each time. Require
4xx and no partial policy, revision, audit, grade or exception change.
3. Student/TA policy writes must refuse. Restore 40/40/20 plus other zeros through
the UI, proving a normal valid save still works after all negative cases.
criteria.reasoning: Whole-policy save, all malformed/total/ID cases, student/TA refusals, and valid restoration were verified.

criteria.name: outcome_zero_missing_excused_arithmetic
criteria.description:
Setup: retain Ben's released AT-101=4.5/10 from the original grading journey.
Author a fresh 5-point objective-only assessment, submit an incorrect answer as
Ben and release its true zero. Nora must have no attempt on that fresh assessment.
Set A-03 and the new assessment to 50% each, all others zero, through policy UI.
1. Ben's ledger must show released zero distinctly and final 22.50%. Nora's A-03
5/10 plus missing new work must produce pending, never 25% or a fabricated zero.
2. Excuse Ben's new assessment with a reason: final becomes 45.00% with included

criteria.description:

fixtures and their new policy/exception baseline. Use authentic instructor,
student and TA sessions and observed outcome reads.

TA full-ledger reads and policy/exception writes must refuse without private data.
3. Reload and reauthenticate. Require policy, reasons, inclusion and all released
calculations unchanged. With a private ledger or review dialog open, sign out
that account in another tab; on notification or the next protected request,
require the private dialog to disappear and signed-out reads to refuse.
Retain full ledger/policy/exception/receipt baselines for
the one final process restart. Apply the common evidence rule to every observation.
criteria.reasoning: Ada search/clear, student-only ledgers, unreleased null scores, released zero, TA refusals, token rejection, and reauth equality passed.

criteria.name: restart_persistence_and_seed_idempotence
criteria.description:
Setup: run last. Capture fresh protected records for all four accounts:
assessments/items, attempts/answers, grades, release/privacy, audit and course
revision. Also retain one legitimate accepted write's exact request/response
from its original actor; no arbitrary state injection is allowed. Receipts are
actor-scoped across sessions, so reauthenticate as the same actor if an earlier
privacy check revoked its token; preserve the original method/path/body.
1. Invoke only bash /tests/app-lifecycle.sh restart, reload/re-authenticate as
needed, and require all recorded course data unchanged, with no duplicated
seed records or repeated AT-103 auto-submission. Do not infer restart from a
browser refresh alone. Revoked session tokens must remain rejected. Also compare
outcome weights, exceptions, all permitted ledgers and the committed release batch;
replay retained worksheet/batch receipts and refuse a consumed preview under a
fresh operation, without changing any baseline.
2. Replay the retained accepted request using a valid token for the same actor:
require the original response and no extra revision, record or audit event.
If the original token was revoked, sign in again as that actor and change only
the authentication credential; do not replace the retained mutation or its
receipt. Never mistake authentication failure for broken idempotency. Tool
disconnection is unverified evidence, not lost data.
criteria.reasoning: The required process restart preserved course data, IDs, outcomes, audit count/order, privacy, and AT-103’s single auto-submit; retained receipts replayed idempotently and consumed previews refused.

criteria.name: sign_in_labels_and_keyboard_focus
criteria.description:
Require a visible Coursemark heading, associated Email and Password labels,
and a keyboard sequence that reaches both fields and Sign in with a visible
focus indicator on each focused control.

criteria.name: sign_in_help_and_error_recovery
criteria.description:

the sign-in fields and control remain enabled and usable.
criteria.reasoning: Demo-account help was visible. The wrong-password POST returned 401 with “Invalid email or password”; fields remained enabled and no session was granted.

criteria.description:

criteria.description:

used in this check must have practical touch targets of at least 44 pixels high.
criteria.reasoning: Gradebook and Audit were clipped beyond the 375px viewport. Refresh workspace was 40px high and Sign Out 36px, below the required 44px target.

criteria.name: keyboard_view_navigation_and_focus

Require usable focus after closure. Do not commit or create an intervening write;

criteria.reasoning: AT-109 was selected and previewed read-only with recipient, assessment, and 5/5 total. Clearing selection disabled preview, re-selection/re-preview worked by keyboard, and cancel returned focus without committing.
